text:
Predicates:
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Classmate(x, michael) ::: x is in Michael's class.
Jumps(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shooter(x) ::: x is a shooter.

Premises:
∀x ∀y ((Man(x) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(x, y)) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
∀x (Classmate(x, michael) → Taller(michael, x)) ::: Michael is a man who is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If person x is taller than person y, and person y is taller than person z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(peter, michael) ∧ Man(peter) ::: Peter is a man who is taller than Michael.
∀x ((Man(x) ∧ ¬Jumps(x)) → CanBlock(michael, x)) ::: Michael can block any shooting from a person as long as the person does not jump when shooting.
¬CanBlock(michael, windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x ((Shooter(x) ∧ Jumps(x)) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.

Conclusion:
CanBlock(peter, windy) ::: Peter can block Windy's shooting.
